reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected GAAP exhibit rows shows a mixed operating picture rather than a clean directional signal. Base-fee and combined advisory/lending revenue rose, and GAAP operating income rose, but the revenue increase was accompanied by a larger increase in total expense, with compensation and general and administration expense both higher. Performance fees rose sharply, which is a lumpy, market- and realization-dependent component; treating that swing as a durable earnings driver would be unsupported by these rows. Below the operating line, net gains on investments fell materially, so pretax income declined even though operating income rose, and consolidated net income declined. Net income attributable to the parent declined by more than consolidated net income because the noncontrolling-interest share of consolidated sponsored investment products increased; the parent-attributable line is the relevant GAAP figure for the listed entity, and the NCI split is an allocation effect, not an operating driver. Income tax expense was lower in absolute terms, but that is consistent with lower pretax income and is not evidence of a reduced tax burden; no effective-rate comparison is established here. End-of-period AUM rose, but AUM is a point-in-time company-reported stock, not a flow, and these rows contain no net inflows, market appreciation, or fee-rate data, so no link between AUM and revenue is established. All comparisons are sequential displayed-value arithmetic, not year-over-year, and no non-GAAP or company-defined measures, guidance, or realized-versus-guided comparisons are present in this extract. Because the selected evidence supports both an improving operating-revenue and operating-income reading and a deteriorating pretax, consolidated, and parent-attributable profit reading, and because the extract lacks the drivers needed to attribute either, the defensible research state is a preserved hold pending fuller filing evidence rather than a conviction change.
